Architecture: This feature adds CI integration for 8 existing test scripts across two workflows. The static tests (no Docker) run in a new lightweight workflow. The Docker-based tests integrate into the existing build-images.yaml as verification jobs between build stages.

Key decisions:
1. verify-container-images.yaml is a separate workflow (not merged into ci.yaml) because it tests container infrastructure, not Go code. Separate workflows provide clear signal in GitHub's check status.
2. verify-base-images is inserted between build-base-images and build-service-images to catch base image issues before they cascade. The dependency chain becomes: build -> verify -> build -> verify.
3. The push-path smoke-test job is renamed to verify-service-images for consistency with verify-base-images.
4. The PR-path inline smoke test is replaced in-place (same step location, same if condition) with verify_keystone.sh to maintain the local --load image pattern.
5. yq installation in verify-container-images.yaml uses the same snap/wget approach as the runner provides for build-images.yaml (ubuntu-latest has yq via snap or we install it).

<go-testing-patterns>
    <pattern name="table-driven-tests">
      Use table-driven tests ([]struct with name, input, expected fields) for functions with multiple input/output combinations.
      Each sub-test via t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) { ... }) for clear failure isolation.
    </pattern>
    <pattern name="test-helpers">
      Use t.Helper() in shared test helper functions so failures report the caller's line number.
      Use t.Cleanup() for teardown instead of defer when cleanup must run after subtests.
    </pattern>
    <pattern name="testify-assertions">
      Prefer testify assert/require for readable assertions: require.NoError, assert.Equal, assert.Contains.
      Use require (fatal) for preconditions, assert (non-fatal) for actual checks.
    </pattern>
    <pattern name="test-file-conventions">
      Test files: *_test.go in the same package (white-box) or _test package (black-box).
      Test functions: TestFunctionName, TestType_MethodName. Subtests via t.Run for variants.
    </pattern>
    <pattern name="mocking">
      Use interfaces for dependencies, inject test doubles. Prefer hand-written fakes over mock frameworks.
      For HTTP: httptest.NewServer. For filesystem: testing/fstest or os.MkdirTemp with t.TempDir().
    </pattern>
    <pattern name="go-test-commands">
      Run tests: go test ./... | Verbose: go test -v ./... | Coverage: go test -cover ./...
      Race detection: go test -race ./... | Specific: go test -run TestName ./pkg/...
    </pattern>
  </go-testing-patterns>

		},
	}

	return c.Status().Update(ctx, obj)
}
